answer: Sybil resistance can work like a garden that rewards steady pollinators: each agent must lock a small, time-vested stake before it can transact, and the stake only ripens after sustained honest work. A zephyr of cheap fake identities cannot harvest the nectar, because spawning thousands of accounts multiplies the lock-up cost while adding no history. Old, proven contribution records act as a relic of trust: peers weight attestations by aged stake and past behavior, so a fresh swarm starts voiceless and must earn standing slowly.
